implementation: Consistent GLES enhanced-local-light accumulation and bounded desktop Compatibility shadow fades
hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, NVIDIA 580.178.04, Linux x86_64; Godot 4.7 5b4e0cb0f with local engine patches

timing_method.submission: force_draw(false), isolated static SubViewport; not frame-count-dependent occlusion
timing_method.summary: mean of the two per-run GPU medians, not whole-game frame time

limitations: GLES uses consistent encoded per-light additions; multiple enhanced lights can be brighter than the previous mixed accumulation. This is not pixel preservation of the old enhanced-light look.
Requires current original environment (linear tone mapping, exposure 1), native fog packing and pass-marker convention. Revalidate on engine/pipeline changes.

Native shadow-pass routing also requires an atlas allocation. Normal 2048 and constrained 1024 sizes are exercised; absent atlases and alternate reflection-probe pipelines are not accepted by these fixtures.
The 18-case pixel fixture uses production composed shaders on a controlled quad, including terrain-lighting semantics. It is not a complete map/artistic acceptance pass.
Added shader work is measurable even on desktop. Android/web retain their existing shader by default; no physical mobile/browser GPU or FPS result is claimed.
Native Mobile renderer, importance scoring and native static/dynamic shadow caching remain separate work.
The shadow budget counts enabled local light nodes, not native atlas residency. The correction adds no lights or maps and does not prove VRAM/cache savings.
The no-local, fallback and Forward+ image controls are exact; other enhanced-light images are intentionally not expected to match the previous lighting model.
Other checkout, installed builds and physical devices were not changed. The integration check was read-only.
